scope: Actual child-process termination at every persistent-controller boundary and inside the fake transport, with checks from a separate parent process

results.preLockScan: No lock or journal; inspect FREE; one follow-on run RELEASED with 1 claim and 1 fake transport
lockedRowInvariants: Lock present and fresh inspect HELD, never FREE
Second run through the same and a fresh controller refused with CONTROLLER_EPOCH_HELD; zero new claims, transports, events or files
At most one CLAIM_INTENT; journal is a valid chain prefix
Held-lock report byte-stable over two reads, releaseAuthorized and executionReady false, writes nothing

heldReportClasses.after-terminal: OBSERVED_STABLE with empty issues while lock PRESENT

rootDecisionOnReplayFailure: The failing check probes process.kill(pid,0) by pid number only at the end of the whole run. Every child had a recorded SIGTERM exit event and an immediate ESRCH at kill time in both runs; the node.exe pid set was unchanged before and after; tasklist showed none of the 17 pids afterwards. Windows reuses pids and each row spawns many short PowerShell probes, so pid reuse is the likely cause; this is not proven. Root classifies it as a harness probe defect, not a controller or orphan failure, and does not count the replay as a clean PASS.

findings.detail: After a kill between the RELEASE terminal record and unlock, the controller holds conservatively, but the held-lock report shows OBSERVED_STABLE with no issue; only lock.presence PRESENT reveals the retained lock.

States after CLAIM_INTENT without a native receipt (including a kill inside transport) are reported only as EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE; in-transport is disk-identical to after-plan, so the report cannot say whether transport began.
End-of-run child liveness probe uses pid only and can report reuse as alive.

limits: Trusted synthetic callbacks and fake IO only; no host effects or operational authority.
Kills only at controller boundaries and inside fake transport; not mid-write, not between native steps without a boundary, not combined with transport/raw/allowlist faults.
Process termination is not OS crash or power loss; no fsync-loss proof.
xs and m4a only; other modes not run.
No reconciliation or unlock API; every killed attempt after lock creation holds indefinitely.
